title: The package that un-delivered itself
blurb: Polls applied stale states and failures looked healthy.
prompt: A delivered shipment flipped back to in transit because a delayed carrier scan arrived after the delivery scan, and a truly stuck shipment looked in transit for days because the draft treated poll failures as no news. Review it, fix it, and prove transitions are monotonic and staleness is visible.
aiNote: The draft writes whatever status the latest poll returns, so an out-of-order scan can regress a terminal shipment, and it maps poll failures to the previous status without any staleness marker, so a stalled carrier feed is invisible.
testIdea: Deliver a shipment then deliver an older in-transit scan and assert the state stays delivered; fail carrier polls for an hour and assert the shipment surfaces as stale; attempt a second active shipment and assert 409.
followUps: How are returns represented in the state machine?
What address data may a timeline ever carry?
